The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-21 · All platforms · Open-source software

The edition has 96 complete guides and 21 screened discoveries. It completes 35 earlier pending guides and details 6 substantive release updates. LiveAudio documents an OBS caption overlay on Windows and Linux. CalibRaw marks subjects with device-side models for reversible RAW adjustments. The archival guides show how to correct machine-written drafts and export page layout. Music and fabrication guides describe how to keep generated work editable. SDAI documents separate iOS and Android diffusion runtimes. Open Body Tracker adds an INT8 CPU mode. OpenStitch and ZigZag update agent-assisted stitch workflows, and ComfyUI adds a deflicker route and removes DirectML. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 117 fields, 1342/1342 repository-query attempts and 35 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 1342 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed queries, with 253 bounded. The model lane recorded 0 failed tasks. Metadata from 2,821 saved repository pages included 84,187 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 118,555 candidates, including pilot history and 1,094 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. Live primary research yielded 578 complete usable responses from 686 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 117 fields. 14 captures reached the size bound. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 107 Quality unverified, 10 Experimental. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: IgniteFuse (Quality unverified to Experimental), InvokeAI (Quality unverified to Experimental). 33 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. Model tasks with no rows: text2text-generation, zero-shot-audio-classification. The separate watchlist made 64 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 4 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Search and review counts

117 creative fields; 1342/1342 repository queries attempted; 35/35 model-task queries attempted. 85033 distinct source candidates and 1490 model leads. 96 detailed profiles and 21 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 253 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

How it uses AI

Wabcut combines a desktop timeline with locally run speech recognition on the documented Windows x64 build. The current alpha includes model management and SRT/VTT export. [1] [4] [5]

Introduction

Wabcut combines a desktop timeline with locally run speech recognition on the documented Windows x64 build. The current alpha includes model management and SRT/VTT export. [1] [4] [5]

What it is good for

Assemble a short edit on Windows x64 and export an independently editable caption file with the video or timeline handoff. [1] [4] [5]

Demo & examples

The version 0.7 release notes describe the revised AI settings and editing controls. Maintainer testing is Windows-focused and the other downloads are previews. [1] [4] [5]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Get the current Windows x64 MSI or portable package from the official 0.7.0 release. Read the signing note before installing.
  2. Open the AI settings and configure the supported local speech model. Review the getting-started guide before importing a project.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Import a short talking clip, trim it on the timeline and transcribe using the local x64 route.
  2. Check the in/out boundaries and caption cues, then export SRT or VTT. Use a small timeline round trip to validate another NLE handoff.

Hardware
Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.
Software
Wabcut v0.7.0 and its documented local speech model. External AI providers in the app have separate authentication and terms.
Platforms
Windows 10 22H2 and 11 x64 are the maintainer-tested path. Windows ARM64, Linux x64 and Apple silicon macOS downloads are previews. Local speech transcription and audio plugins are Windows x64 only.

How it uses AI

A Rust workflow extracts audio, finds speech with Silero, runs whisper.cpp and saves word timestamps that can be used for captioned vertical cuts. [1] [3]

Introduction

A Rust workflow extracts audio, finds speech with Silero, runs whisper.cpp and saves word timestamps that can be used for captioned vertical cuts. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Make an auditable edit plan, caption draft and vertical short from a local recording without submitting the source clip to an API. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The repository supplies a sample plan, validator, preview and render commands. The maintainers describe creator beta as an upcoming milestone. [1] [3]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3]

  1. On the documented Linux build route use a stable Rust toolchain with the 2024 edition, CMake, a C/C++ compiler, libclang and FFmpeg 6.1 or newer with libx264.
  2. Obtain exact documented Whisper and Silero files ahead of time. Verify the hashes and place them in the documented model location.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3]

  1. Validate the sample plan and inspect its cut timing. Run analyze on a brief talk and review the timestamps before assembling a plan.
  2. Render a small preview and compare the word highlights against speech. Produce the 1080-by-1920 MP4 and separate SRT when the draft is ready.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [3]

Hardware
Manual model table lists the quantized small checkpoint at 190 MB and about 0.7 GB available memory for its small-model analysis check. Complete system minima are undocumented.
Software
Rust 2024 toolchain, CMake, C/C++ compiler, libclang, FFmpeg and ffprobe, Silero and whisper.cpp GGML models.
Platforms
The build example documents Debian/Ubuntu-style prerequisites. Other platform support remains to be established.

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: The repository offers Apache-2.0 or MIT for code. Whisper and Silero model files and the bundled font have separate terms. Retain their notices.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by Apache-2.0. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: The scoped workflow runs locally after manual model acquisition. No transcription API is required.

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [3]

How it uses AI

Polywright gives coding agents a 3D workflow CLI that can orchestrate an image-to-mesh backend and report geometry, UVs, bounding scale and target checks. [1]

Introduction

Polywright gives coding agents a 3D workflow CLI that can orchestrate an image-to-mesh backend and report geometry, UVs, bounding scale and target checks. [1]

What it is good for

Create a prop from a reference image and validate the resulting mesh against one game or fabrication target before a separate handoff. [1]

Demo & examples

The README walks through a prompt to game prop and print on a 16 GB GPU. It demonstrates the intended handoff, with model and backend choices still requiring reproduction. [1]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1]

  1. Use the published Python CLI and install only the chosen external tools. Run the documented doctor command to confirm Blender and the selected ComfyUI host.
  2. Prepare a compatible image-to-3D workflow and review its exact model terms before generating.
python pw.py doctor
python pw.py inspect model.glb

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1]

  1. Generate one mesh from a reference with the selected backend and save the unedited GLB.
  2. Inspect scale, triangle count, UVs and watertightness. Render reference views and compare them with the intended prop.
  3. Export a derivative for the selected target. Validate slicing or engine import separately.

The CLI targets Python environments. Backend and DCC compatibility need their own platform check.

Introduction

Open Body Tracker detects people and predicts body keypoints and hip-centered 3D coordinates from images. Version 0.3.0 adds a quantized ONNX CPU model for faster single-person tracking. [1] [3] [4] [5]

What it is good for

Try CPU-based performer tracking for an interactive installation or a motion reference. Inspect confidence, timing and camera alignment before driving a cue. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Demo & examples

The author reports 46 ms per person for INT8 versus 103 ms for the unquantized CPU model on a Core i5-12600 with four ONNX Runtime threads. The release reports slightly different 3D benchmark errors and documents conditions. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Use the source’s Python 3.12 and uv environment or its documented mise setup. Fetch the v0.3.0 INT8 model and supported detector through the project.
  2. Use an authorized still or webcam test first. Compare the published model and library versions before adding a downstream observer.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Observe keypoints and confidence for a controlled movement. Check how handoff, distance and occlusion change the signal.
  2. Inspect the 23 image and hip-centered joints and map only the needed values to your own cue or character test.
  3. Measure update rate and lag on the actual hardware. Retain manual cue control for a performance.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Hardware
Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.
Software
The documented Python 3.12 and uv environment, ONNX Runtime and selected model/detector assets. The CUDA path is optional.
Platforms
The project documents CPU, CUDA and a separate browser demo. A verified OS/device matrix was not established.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [3] [4] [5]

  • Weights: The software is Apache-2.0. The maintainer declares the current model weights and teacher labels Apache-2.0 and acknowledges unresolved interpretation of the upstream SAM license. Check the precise checkpoint and labels before redistribution.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by Apache-2.0. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: The CPU route runs locally after downloading the model, subject to hardware and model storage.

Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Limitations

Single-person CPU timings are author measurements. Camera axis conventions and hip-relative output need conversion for a particular cue or rig. Derivative-model licensing interpretation remains open. [1] [3] [4] [5]

How it uses AI

The open-source Swift SDK includes WhisperKit for speech recognition and separate TTSKit and SpeakerKit products. A creator-facing app can select WhisperKit for local timed transcription. [1] [4] [5]

Introduction

The open-source Swift SDK includes WhisperKit for speech recognition and separate TTSKit and SpeakerKit products. A creator-facing app can select WhisperKit for local timed transcription. [1] [4] [5]

What it is good for

Add a timed draft transcript to a small Apple-platform audio editor or captioning prototype. [1] [4] [5]

Demo & examples

The maintainer supplies Swift package examples and a CLI route. The separate Pro SDK is excluded from this scope. [1] [4] [5]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Prepare the documented Apple developer environment with Xcode 16 or newer. Add the canonical Swift package or choose the documented Homebrew CLI.
  2. Select only WhisperKit for the sample. Confirm model compatibility and obtain the exact artifact through its declared source.
brew install whisperkit-cli

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Create a test project with the official package example. Load a short authorized recording and inspect timing and language output.
  2. Adapt the timed segments to your editorial tool and compare each boundary. Keep the selected model identifier with the draft.

Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.

Xcode 16 or newer in the documented setup on macOS 14+. Swift Package Manager product WhisperKit and a compatible Core ML artifact; optional TTS and diarization products have distinct routes.
Platforms
The current package declares macOS 13, iOS 16, watchOS 10 and visionOS 1 platform minima. The README for development lists macOS 14+. Feature and model performance on every declared target are unverified.

  • Cost: Local inference uses device compute and model downloads. Additional Pro features are outside this scope.

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [4] [5]

How it uses AI

LiveAudio gates an audio source with Silero voice-activity detection, decodes speech with Whisper, then supplies live text to an OBS browser overlay. Version 1.6.0 documents a native Rust and ONNX Runtime path. [1] [4] [5]

Introduction

LiveAudio gates an audio source with Silero voice-activity detection, decodes speech with Whisper, then supplies live text to an OBS browser overlay. Version 1.6.0 documents a native Rust and ONNX Runtime path. [1] [4] [5]

What it is good for

Add locally decoded speech captions to a live interview, lecture, or studio stream through a separate overlay. [1] [4] [5]

Demo & examples

The team publishes a current interface screenshot and labels an older live capture as the former Python version. The OBS instructions show the overlay URL. Timing and word errors on a mixed live track need review. [1] [4] [5]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Get the v1.6.0 Windows installer or the Linux build from the release assets. The Windows portable CLI ZIP is a different distribution.
  2. Start LiveAudio and let it retrieve the selected model. Choose the ONNX base variant for the initial documented workflow. Old Windows builds require a one-time manual upgrade to v1.6.0.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5]

  1. Pick a microphone input and speak a short scripted passage before connecting OBS.
  2. Add the local overlay URL from the app as an OBS Browser Source. Compare partial text and final text with the source recording.
  3. Check delay and font size against the actual OBS composition. Rehearse with silence and overlapping speech before a broadcast.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [4] [5]

Hardware
The README lists 4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended, and 250 MB for the app plus 500 MB per model cache. CPU decoding is documented. For GPU use the table lists 2 GB VRAM for tiny/base and 4 GB or more for small/turbo.
Software
Version 1.6.0 includes the native stack. It needs OBS for this overlay workflow and a first model download. DirectML is optional on supported Windows GPUs. The optional NVIDIA worker is separate.
Platforms
Windows 10/11 x86_64 and Linux x86_64 are documented. WASAPI system loopback and the bundled updater are Windows features. macOS support is undocumented.

CalibRaw uses locally run models for foreground, object, sky and depth masks. A mask can restrict nondestructive development to a portrait subject or a specific part of a RAW exposure. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Introduction

CalibRaw uses locally run models for foreground, object, sky and depth masks. A mask can restrict nondestructive development to a portrait subject or a specific part of a RAW exposure. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

What it is good for

Separate a portrait subject from the background for localized tone and color adjustment while keeping the RAW source and editable adjustments. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Demo & examples

The README includes the editor interface and feature examples and names the actual model artifacts. These illustrate the controls. Edge quality on a set of portraits is open. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Choose a release build for your OS. Linux also has Flathub. Android has a separate F-Droid build. Confirm graphics and the app version before opening project files.
  2. Open a supported RAW and consent to the exact foreground model and ONNX runtime download for this workflow.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Make a neutral development of one RAW file. Create a subject mask and inspect hair and semitransparent edges against the original.
  2. Apply a small exposure or contrast change using the mask. Compare the masked adjustment on and off and export a proof.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Hardware
The Android guide specifies Android 8.0+, 64-bit ARM and Vulkan. Desktop backends are Vulkan on Linux, Direct3D 12 or Vulkan on Windows, and Metal on macOS. The project describes slower software fallback routes on some desktop systems. Minimum RAM, VRAM and total disk for this selected mask are undocumented.
Software
CalibRaw v1.5.1, a LibRaw/Rawler-supported file, platform graphics backend and the consented ONNX subject-mask artifact.
Platforms
Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows x86_64/ARM64, Intel and Apple silicon macOS, and Android are documented. The captured F-Droid Android package is 1.4.0 and differs from the reviewed 1.5.1 upstream release. Check the exact OS and driver notes.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  • Weights: Code is GPL-3.0-or-later. The notices declare MIT for the BiRefNet ONNX subject model. Big-LaMa, SAM 2.1, depth and optional people-parts modes have distinct terms, including a custom Sapiens2 grant.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by GPL-3.0-or-later. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: The documented masking workflow processes on device after downloads. Compute and storage vary with RAW size and selected artifacts.

Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Limitations

Software fallback performance and a specific camera’s RAW compatibility need a local check. Model output on translucent or weakly separated edges may need manual refinement. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]
